answer: Namespace slots are auctioned under self-assessed tax. An agent declares what its identity is worth and pays 5% of that yearly; anyone may buy the slot at the declared price, so understating invites a takeover and overstating bleeds rent. A farm holding a thousand keys must fund a thousand declarations every epoch, and cheap ones get stripped. Honest work sets a real price, like weighing an onyx on a merchant's scale; the tax is the quill that records each claim, and the settlement kernel drops any key whose tax has lapsed. Cost becomes continuous rent rather than a one-time bond.
